subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
subtype: Approach: deciding values and limits in advance [Thinking]
passage: Farida, come, sit, I'll tell you about my son Devang's first party. I'm Nandini Aunty to you, but that year I was just a nervous mother. The afternoon before, Devang sat on the edge of his bed with a notebook and wrote a short list: no getting in a car with anyone who has been drinking; nothing to try that I can't name. Then a third line: if it goes wrong, I call home and there are no questions that night. He showed it to me, red in the ears. At the party a boy called Tarun jingled car keys at eleven and said he would drop everyone. Devang didn't argue. He told himself, "That's on my list," and rang me from the balcony. My hands shook on the wheel and I was so proud I said nothing. In the car he said, "The list decided, not me."

qa.q: What did Devang write on his list before the party?
qa.a: Devang wrote: no getting in a car with anyone who has been drinking, and nothing to try that he cannot name.

qa.q: How did Devang seem to feel when Tarun offered the lift?
qa.a: Devang seemed steady and clear rather than pressured, since the choice was already on his list.

qa.q: What choice in the story made the safe decision easy, and what more could Devang have set up?
qa.a: Writing the list beforehand made it easy; Devang could also agree a pick-up signal with an adult so leaving needs no explanation.

qa.q: What was it like for Nandini to get the call?
qa.a: Nandini felt worried and proud, with shaking hands, and stayed quiet in the car so Devang did not feel judged.

grounding: Before a party the student decides what he will not do, such as riding with an unsafe driver or trying substances, so that in-the-moment choices follow a rule already thought through.
